title: The Real Culprit
text: Phew… Well, my Father is leading me right into the room. So I follow him inside and take a seat.
“So? Motoyasu, what are you hiding?”
“Big Sister, is anyone eavesdropping on us?”
I ask my Big Sister.
“Big Sister? You mean me?”
“Since I’m Filo-tan’s Big Sister, that makes me your Big Sister, doesn’t it?”
“Seriously, what is this guy?”
“Huh? Um… I don’t think anyone’s hiding…”
I guess that means we’re safe, right? Just to be sure, I’ll cast Magic.
“If anyone’s hiding, you’d better come out right now—or I’ll burn you to a crisp, friend or foe!”
With that declaration, I cast Magic.
“Motoyasu, what are you doing?!”
“Liberation Fireflash X!”
With a flash, I formed a Magic spell that seared everything within the room. After that, I used a variation of the Magic spell to soundproof the room.
“…I sense some Magic power, but I don’t see any particular changes.”
“It’s a Magic spell that’ll burn anyone hiding here.”
“Is there such Magic…? So you don’t want anyone eavesdropping?”
“Where should I start? If I go from the beginning, it’ll be quite a long story—do you want to hear it?”
“Just the highlights… I’d like to hear those, but if that’s all, I’ll probably end up completely lost.”
My Father thought for a moment before speaking.

“I trusted you for the time being, and as a result, I was able to make that woman pay for her deeds. I’ll at least hear you out… All right. Why did you go about this in such a roundabout way? Especially that farce. What was the point of that?”
“It’s because I came from the future of this world. That’s why I have knowledge of the future.”
My father’s eyes narrowed, as if filled with suspicion.
“Even if we assume you’re right and you do have knowledge of the future, why did you do something like that?”
“It’s because if I do anything different from what happens in the future, I won’t be able to make the Crimson Swine face his retribution.”
At this point, my father stopped. A question mark floated across his face.
“Crimson Swine?”
“A Crimson Swine is a Crimson Swine, you see.”
“Raphtalia, I have absolutely no idea what this guy is talking about. Do you understand?”
“Um… judging by the word ‘retribution,’ maybe the Pope…? And based on the hair color, could it be the person who passed away today?”
“Motoyasu, is that right?”
“That’s right. He’s a fat, bloated pig, after all.”

“You’ve been calling him a pig and things like that from time to time… so that’s what it means. Raphtalia has also been saying you’ve been acting strange since around the second wave—does this have anything to do with it?”
“Of course it does. I entered this loop just a little before the second wave hit.”
Perhaps he finds something convincing about it; this Father seems to grasp things faster than the one from when the loop first started. That just shows how much trust he has in Big Sister.
“So, that ‘pretending to be asleep’ thing that Raphtalia was wondering about…”
“Of course, it didn’t hurt a bit.”
It didn’t bother him at all. Round and round and round…
“Did you do anything to that guy named Glass?”
“As backup, I shrunk my spear and hit him in the leg with it.”
“So that’s why he was limping…”
I could have actually taken him down, but I held back because doing so might have changed the future in various ways. After all, it seems he was an ally in the first world.
“That makes sense. With all these enhancements, he should be stronger—there’s no way he’d lose to that Glass guy I barely managed to drive off.”
“This lady here…”
Big Sister is pressing her hand to her forehead as if in despair.
“So… when you say ‘making the Bitch pay,’ you don’t mean I’m going to punish her by making her change her name, do you?”
“Of course not… That woman called you—”
“Wait. Did you just call me ‘Father’?”
Huh? My father is making a really grim face.
“I did think it was odd to call her ‘Big Sister’ just because she’s Filo’s older sister. How did the guy who used to call her ‘Raphtalia-chan’ end up doing that?”
“That’s because Filo-tan saved me.”

Ah… I can still vividly recall that moment. That image of her—how she kicked me and scolded me for being so foolish, and then comforted me when I was depressed over the fact that I’d been tricked by that pig.
“Since you came from the future and mentioned ‘loops’… Motoyasu, how many loops is this?”
“I’ve lost count. It ended once, but now it’s starting all over again.”
“It ended once? And yet you’ve looped again?”
We had this same exchange when the loop started all over again, didn’t we?
“Filo-tan saved my heart. That’s why I affectionately call you ‘Father,’ since you’re Filo-tan’s father.”
My father put his hand over his mouth and made a grim face.
“Raphtalia, do you think it’s okay to kick this guy out of the room without even hearing him out?”
“Um… I think we should at least hear him out. After all, it’s a fact that I was being manipulated by this person.”
“I see. Anyway, so Filo did something to you, and because of that, you’ve fallen for her and are calling me and Raphtalia by these strange names, right?”
“That’s right. I’m devoted solely to Filo-tan.”
Second on the list is the great Filolial-sama. But what should I do about Fleon-chan? I’m satisfied just that she’s grown up safely.
“And yet, you seem to be scared of Filo…”
“Ugh…”
He’s hitting a sore spot. I’ll just let that one slide.
“A-anyway, after going through a lot, I realized the truth, and now I’m helping my Father across all these loops.”
“…Sigh. It sounds like a complicated situation, but I get it. So, what were you planning to do to the Bitch? She died from the poison she administered herself… No, surely you didn’t—”
Just as I expected from my Father! It seems you’ve pieced together the truth from the context.

“You’ve figured it out, haven’t you? In the original timeline, the poison was only strong enough to require her to be taken to a clinic for treatment to stay alive. But I gave it a little extra kick!”
“No way…”
Father and Big Sister are speechless. I nod firmly.
“Who’d have thought there was such a real culprit… Should I tell the Queen?”
“The only pity is that the poison’s effect was far stronger than I’d imagined. I would’ve loved to watch him make an even bigger fool of himself.”
“…What on earth happened to make this womanizer end up like this?　Well, knowing that woman, I’m sure all sorts of things happened…”
My father has an indescribable look on his face. That’s right. All sorts of things happened. In conclusion, the Crimson Swine must die.
“Since we entered this loop around the time of the second wave, does that mean what happened before that is irrelevant?”

“That’s news to me, too. I’d heard there was a prince—the Crimson Swine’s younger brother—but I didn’t know he’d died from the deadly Uroboros poison. Either way, as Father taught me: if someone hits you, hit them back.”
“Who told you to take it that far…? Or—did someone poison you or something?”
“It wasn’t me—it was Fleon-chan.”
“That flying, brainwashed Filolial? I remember you used to envy the fact that Filo could fly.”
I nod. With this, I’ve finally avenged Fleon-chan’s unfulfilled wishes from the first world.

“In the first world, I learned that Filo-tan, in her angelic form, was a Filolial, and since my Father could do it, I wanted a Filolial too. Back then, Crimson Swine brought me an egg, and I named it ‘Fleon’ and raised it. But Fleon-chan died before she could grow up. His excuse was something like, ‘Her body couldn’t handle the growth,’ wasn’t it?”
“So… she’s now manipulating Itsuki with seemingly excessive energy… I see. If I imagine that woman—what if Motoyasu had gotten his hands on a Filo—it’s exactly the kind of thing she’d do.”
“You actually buy that?”
“Raphtalia, think about it carefully. It’s that woman, after all. Can you really say it’s impossible?”
“Well…”
“Well, this alone isn’t enough to prove Motoyasu’s side of the story is correct, but there are parts that make sense. She took down the Pope instantly, as if he were nothing.”
It’s nice that my father is so understanding about these things.

“Above all… she mentioned the name of a shield that Motoyasu shouldn’t have known. I thought maybe she knew it from the game, but even that doesn’t add up. It’s hard to say her claim of coming from the future lacks credibility.”
That’s one of Father’s good qualities—he’s quick to cut through the nonsense.
“Anyway, so we’re saying you did all this just to make it look like that woman died as a result of her own actions, right?”
“That’s right. I’ll answer any questions about what happened afterward as best I can. After all, our objective has been achieved, and Fleon-chan’s safety has been secured.”
“…Alright, then. So, in the future you know about, what events are supposed to happen originally? ”

“Well… back when I was foolish, I figured out what was going on when Crimson Swine was carried into the clinic. Just like when I challenged my Father to a duel over Big Sister, I tried to challenge him to a duel to remove Crimson Swine’s slave mark—but the Queen refused.”

“I’d have liked to see that. I’m kind of jealous, actually. From my perspective, it’s kind of creepy—like my archenemy, the guy I wanted to teach a lesson, turned into this mysteriously obedient servant.”
My Father furrows his brow and lets out a sigh. His reaction here is similar to that of my Father in the first world.
“Hey, Motoyasu, spin around three times and let out a cry.”
“Spin, spin, spin! It’s a ‘Kue’!”
Obeying my Father’s command, I spin gracefully and strike the pose of the raging Filolial-sama! It’s a ‘Kue’!
What do you think, Father? This Filolial-sama pose, honed in the Colosseum, is pretty cool, isn’t it?
“Haa…”
“Naofumi-sama, if you’re going to sigh, why not just not give the order in the first place?”
“I was testing to see if you’d take it seriously. I don’t know… I wonder what I was even working so hard for?”
“Let’s just say this is also thanks to Filo and Naofumi-sama for taking care of the Spear Hero…”
“By the way, my Big Sister used to get really mad at me. She’d get angry and say, ‘Even if it weren’t my Big Sister, Father could get over it with any other slave!’”
“Lord Naofumi, let’s kick this guy out!”
Oh? My Big Sister’s radiating killing intent! Did I say something rude? The Big Sister in my head is yelling, “Why do you always have to say unnecessary things!” But it’s the truth.

“Wait, wait… Why bother taking Motoyasu seriously? Even if it’s true, it’s just part of one of the countless loops we’re in. I’m sure there are examples like that. So, Motoyasu, what are the other slaves besides Raphtalia like?”
“A rabbit and a lizardman.”
“…Ah, those guys. I remember them. The possibility of buying them… that might very well be a real possibility.”
“Naofumi-sama…”
Big Sister looks heartbroken. I should comfort her and earn some brownie points here.
“Big Sister, please don’t be so down.”
“Whose fault is this?!”

“That loop happened when Ren and Itsuki went through it—back when I didn’t help frame my Father. I wanted to save my Father, but I couldn’t break out of the loop without reuniting with Filo-tan, so I had to steel my heart and leave it to them. That’s when I found out.”
“So that’s the one where you broke out of the loop once… You got to see Filo, right? Why are you stuck in the loop again?”
“I don’t know.”

Rival said he’d look into it too—I wonder how that’s going? I feel like he explained something… while I was in shock, but my memory’s a bit fuzzy. It wasn’t really the time to focus on that, after all.

“By the way, when I helped out and Father missed his chance to buy a slave, Big Sister’s older sister and Father met and saved the day. That’s how we managed to pull through that last chance. And that’s how I somehow managed to meet Filo-tan.”

“I kind of feel like I want to hear the details of exactly how and why I got to meet Filo, but if I asked, it’d probably be morning before I finished, so I’ll let it go. Raphtalia, do you have an older sister?”
My Father and the others have this exchange all the time. Well, that just goes to show what an untrustworthy guy I used to be. Didn’t Filo-tan say it herself? “Be sincere,” she said.
“Um… if there’s anyone I look up to and call ‘sister’… I suppose it would be Sadeena-neesan? Yes. We’re not related by blood, but because she was close with my parents, she treated me like a sister.”

“She’s in Zeltoble now, isn’t she? I sent my father-in-law and the others to Zeltoble to get some rest… so if you happen to run into a woman who’s drinking heavily at a tavern or something, that’s her.”
Judging from the loops so far…
“…Could it be her? There was this weird guy I met when I left Raphtalia and the others waiting at the inn to gather intel.”
“That’s impressive. Just as I’d expect from my Father.”
I remember that when I described her characteristics and asked him to bring her to me, he actually did. My Father and my Big Sister’s older sister share a mysterious connection, after all.
“Sadeena is in Zeltoble…”
“Should I go pick her up right now?”
“It’s already late at night, and I’m exhausted from everything that’s happened, so I’d prefer to do it another day. I spoke with her briefly, but that woman is the kind who wears you out.”
“Sadeena-nee is a cheerful person who acts a bit frivolous, though…”
My Father seems quite tired.
“Above all, I have a Class Up coming up tomorrow. I’d like to get some rest early.”
Oh? A Class Up… Come to think of it, I haven’t met Filolial-sama yet.
“I’d prefer if you waited to do the Class Up. If possible, I’d recommend doing it after you’ve met Filolial-sama.”
